### Project Name

Prismor

### Project Description

Prismor is an Apache-2.0, self-hosted control plane for AI agents. It performs **tool call interception** between an agent and the tools it uses. Before a tool executes, Prismor evaluates the call against **policy-as-code** and returns an allow, block, transform, or approval verdict.

The project began in early 2026 as `immunity-agent` on PyPI. Version 1.13.0 renamed the package to `prismor` in June 2026. The prior package remains a compatibility shim for existing users.

Prismor covers three primary enforcement surfaces through one policy engine:

- Coding-agent hooks for agent frameworks and coding harnesses
- In-process SDK adapters for production agent frameworks
- An MCP Gateway that evaluates downstream `tools/call` requests before forwarding them and scans tool results before they reach the model

Operators use **observe mode** to measure impact before rollout and **enforce mode** to block an action before execution. Policies are versioned YAML, reviewed as code, and can be applied at organization, project, repository, and session scope.

### Alignment with AAIF Mission

AAIF projects make agentic systems interoperable and safe to use across vendors and runtimes. Prismor supplies the runtime enforcement layer for that work. It evaluates an agent's action before tool execution and applies policy independently of model-context instructions.

The project is useful where agents can read private data, use credentials, call external services, modify source code, or invoke MCP tools. A policy can block a risky tool call, require human approval, redact a result, or record the decision for review. Signed audit trails and attestation bundles give operators evidence of the controls applied to a deployment.

Prismor is licensed under Apache-2.0. Its policy schema, enforcement logic, integration adapters, security reporting process, and governance documents are public.

### Relation to Existing AAIF Projects

Prismor complements agent frameworks and protocols by governing the actions they execute.

- **MCP:** Prismor's MCP Gateway fronts downstream MCP servers. It applies policy before forwarding `tools/call` requests and scans returned content before it enters an agent context. Prismor does not change the MCP protocol or propose a competing protocol.
- **Agent frameworks and coding agents:** Prismor provides adapters and hooks that let an existing agent framework retain its own execution model while using a shared policy engine for tool calls.
- **Agent gateways:** Network gateways govern traffic between systems. Prismor governs tool execution from inside supported agent runtimes and MCP clients. The layers can be deployed together when an organization needs both network controls and runtime controls.

The intended AAIF contribution is a vendor-neutral enforcement component that works with existing AAIF protocols, runtimes, and infrastructure.

### Example Use Cases and Evidence of Adoption

#### Use cases

1. A developer starts a coding agent in **observe mode**, reviews findings, then moves selected rules to **enforce mode** for destructive commands, secret access, untrusted content, and network egress.
2. A platform team wraps a LangChain, OpenAI Agents SDK, or other supported application with a Prismor adapter. The team attributes actions to the end user and applies policy before the application executes a tool.
3. A security team places existing MCP servers behind the MCP Gateway, applies one policy to downstream tools, and reviews scanned tool results and decisions.
4. A compliance team verifies a signed audit trail and produces an attestation bundle that records policy posture, agent inventory, and the trail anchor.

### Governance Model

Prismor has a public governance model covering roles, promotion from contributor to reviewer and maintainer, lazy consensus, voting, security-sensitive changes, release authority, and the separation between the open-source project and the Prismor company: <https://github.com/PrismorSec/prismor/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md>

The governance model defines the process for nominating and approving additional reviewers and maintainers.

### CI/CD & Release Workflow

GitHub Actions runs three required workflows on every push and pull request:

- `oss-guard.yml` scans tracked files for secrets, private signing material, and premium-feed content, then runs its guard tests
- `security-regression.yml` verifies the integration registry and runs the cloaking and policy suite on Linux. Its Windows job installs and dispatches hooks under cmd.exe, PowerShell, and Git Bash, then runs a non-interactive setup from a built wheel
- `static-analysis.yml` runs Ruff for syntax and undefined-name errors, plus Bandit SAST at medium severity and above across `prismor` and `adapters`

Release automation uses two separate workflows. A `v*` tag builds the `prismor` package and the `immunity-agent` redirect package, creates the GitHub release, and publishes both packages to PyPI through trusted publishing. An `adapters-v*` tag or a manual run builds and publishes the TypeScript `vercel-ai` and `mastra` adapters to npm when `NPM_TOKEN` is configured.

The public release history records six releases from `v1.50.0` to `v1.54.1` during 11 to 17 September 2026. The contribution guide defines local validation and the pull-request process:

<https://github.com/PrismorSec/prismor/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md>

### Public-Facing Contribution Process for Specifications

The public contribution process uses GitHub issues, pull requests, discussions, and review. Contributors begin by checking the documented extension points. Detection rules belong in YAML, integration work follows the integration registry, and material new surfaces start as a public issue labeled `proposal`.

The contribution guide describes development setup, test gates, security-sensitive areas, pull-request requirements, and private vulnerability reporting:

<https://github.com/PrismorSec/prismor/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md>

The governance document defines how contributors become reviewers and maintainers, including the approval process and decision rights:

<https://github.com/PrismorSec/prismor/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md>

### External Project Dependencies

The core runtime has two required direct dependencies:

| Dependency | Purpose | License |
|---|---|---|
| PyYAML | Policy parsing | MIT |
| tomli, for Python below 3.11 | TOML parsing | MIT |

Optional extras install only when an operator selects a signing, semantic-guard, or framework adapter integration. `cryptography` is licensed Apache-2.0 OR BSD-3-Clause and `litellm`, `langchain-core`, `openai-agents`, `pydantic-ai-slim`, `autogen-core`, `semantic-kernel`, and `claude-agent-sdk` are MIT-licensed according to their current PyPI metadata. The full optional dependency set, version constraints, and project links are in `pyproject.toml`:

<https://github.com/PrismorSec/prismor/blob/main/pyproject.toml>

Before submission, Prismor will publish a versioned SPDX or CycloneDX SBOM that records every direct and transitive dependency, including optional framework extras, with its resolved license. Add that public link here before filing.

### Leadership Team & Decision Process

The maintainer group sets project direction, merges code, cuts releases, signs the advisory feed, appoints reviewers and maintainers, and changes governance. Routine changes use lazy consensus in public issues and pull requests. Security-sensitive changes require a maintainer and a second reviewer or maintainer. Governance changes require a two-thirds maintainer majority.

The complete decision process is public at:

<https://github.com/PrismorSec/prismor/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md>

### Roadmap

Prismor seeks entry as a **Growth** project.

| Period | Milestone | Measure |
|---|---|---|
| First 90 days | Publish a project health report | Maintainers, contributor activity, release cadence, deployment references, and security response metrics |
| Months 3 to 6 | Publish interoperability and conformance priorities | Public issues and tests for supported agent runtimes, MCP Gateway behavior, and policy-event compatibility |
| Months 6 to 12 | Expand the reviewer and maintainer group | Public nominations and role changes under the governance process, with organization diversity reported quarterly |
| Months 6 to 12 | Publish release and supply-chain evidence | Versioned SBOMs, release notes, security advisories, and OpenSSF status for each supported release |

### Security

Prismor has an OpenSSF Best Practices Passing badge:

<https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/14922>

The project publishes a security policy with private GitHub advisory and email reporting channels, a 48-hour acknowledgement target, a seven-day target for critical fixes, and a 30-day target for high and medium fixes:

<https://github.com/PrismorSec/prismor/blob/main/SECURITY.md>

The public CI gates include secret and signing-key protection, security regressions, integration-registry validation, Ruff, and Bandit. Security-sensitive policy, hook, cloaking, feed, key, and CI changes receive stricter review under the governance model.
